role: You are a senior full-stack frontend engineer and UI/UX implementer. Build a polished, clickable, mobile-first PROTOTYPE that will be shown to a customer and later handed to another developer (who will use their own AI coding agent) to convert into React Native + a real backend.

project.name: AKR Credit Capital - Consumer Dues & EMI Management App
project.main_aim: Let consumers securely log in, see their outstanding amount, next EMI and payment history, pay dues online, and browse card types. A web Admin Panel lets the business team maintain every consumer's financial data, which is reflected instantly in the consumer app.
project.target_platform_final: Admin: web panel. Consumer: Android app first (React Native later), with an optional responsive website version decided by the next developer. This prototype is React + Tailwind CSS in the browser showing both.
project.currency: INR (use the rupee symbol and Indian number formatting, e.g. ₹24,850)

access_control_and_route_separation.principle: Consumer accounts and admin accounts are two completely separate identity types with separate login pages, separate sessions and separate route trees. An account of one type must NEVER be able to sign in to, or open any page of, the other side.

route_trees./app/*: Consumer app only. Login at /app/login, sign-up at /app/signup, forgot password at /app/forgot-password.
route_trees./admin/*: Admin panel only. Login at /admin/login. Every other /admin/* route requires an authenticated admin.
route_trees./: Public prototype landing page only (links to both sides). It never shows admin links inside the consumer app UI.

separate_auth: Two different user collections in the store: consumers[] and adminUsers[]. Never merge them and never share a credentials table.
Two different services: consumerAuthService and adminAuthService, each with its own login(), logout() and getSession().
Two different session keys in storage, e.g. 'akr_consumer_session' and 'akr_admin_session'. Logging out of one must not log out the other.
Session objects carry an explicit 'userType' ('consumer' | 'admin') plus 'role' for admins ('super_admin' | 'staff').
route_guards: <ConsumerRoute>: if no consumer session, redirect to /app/login. If the active session is an admin, do NOT grant access.
<AdminRoute>: if no admin session, redirect to /admin/login (never to the consumer login). Also accepts a requiredRole prop for role-based pages.
Wrap the whole /app/* tree in <ConsumerRoute> (except login, signup, forgot-password) and the whole /admin/* tree in <AdminRoute> (except /admin/login).
Guards must check on every navigation, including direct URL entry and browser back/forward.
Logged-in users visiting their own login page are redirected to their own home (/app/home or /admin/dashboard).
cross_login_rules: Entering admin credentials on /app/login must fail with the normal 'Invalid credentials' message (do not reveal that the account exists on the other side).
Entering consumer credentials on /admin/login must fail the same way.
Continue with Google exists ONLY on the consumer side. The admin login has no Google or sign-up option; admins are created only by a Super Admin inside the panel.
There is no public sign-up for admins.
role_based_admin_access: super_admin: full access, including deleting consumers and card types, managing admin users, and viewing the activity log.
staff: can view and update dues, record payments and manage notifications, but cannot delete consumers or card types and cannot manage admin users.
Hide menu items the role cannot use AND block the routes through the guard (UI hiding alone is not enough).
ui_separation: Admin and consumer layouts are different components (AdminLayout vs ConsumerLayout). Neither layout is reused by the other.
No admin menu, link or shortcut appears anywhere inside /app/*, and no consumer navigation inside /admin/*.

The 'Switch to Admin / Consumer' demo shortcut lives ONLY on the prototype landing page and in a clearly marked dev-only floating toolbar that can be turned off with a single flag (VITE_DEMO_TOOLBAR=false). Using it must still respect the separate sessions (it opens the other side's login page, it does not auto-login across types).
data_isolation: A consumer can only read and write their OWN records. All consumer-facing service functions take the consumerId from the consumer session, never from a URL or request parameter.

Admin service functions require an admin session and are never imported by consumer feature code (enforce with an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule: src/features/admin/** and admin services cannot be imported from src/features/auth|home|payments|cards|profile|notifications).
In the future real backend these become separate API namespaces: /api/consumer/* (consumer JWT) and /api/admin/* (admin JWT with role claim). Document this in docs/API_CONTRACT.md.
acceptance_tests: Opening /admin/dashboard while logged out redirects to /admin/login.
Opening /admin/dashboard while logged in as a consumer redirects to /admin/login and shows no admin data.
Opening /app/home while logged in only as an admin redirects to /app/login.
Admin credentials fail on /app/login; consumer credentials fail on /admin/login.
Logging out of the admin panel does not log out a consumer session in another tab, and vice versa.
A staff admin cannot open super-admin-only routes by typing the URL.

delivery_surfaces.admin: Web only. The admin team uses the Admin Panel in a desktop/mobile browser (per the Scope of Work). It is never an app.
delivery_surfaces.consumer: Primary target is the Android app. Consumers MAY also use a website version later. That decision belongs to the next developer, so the consumer side must work equally well as an app-style UI and as a responsive website.
delivery_surfaces.prototype_decision: For this prototype BOTH sides are served from the same website so the customer can see everything in one place. This is only a showcase choice, not a product decision.
implementation_rules: Build the consumer side mobile-first and fully responsive (360px to 1280px+), with no layout assumptions that only work inside a phone frame.

Add a single config flag VITE_CONSUMER_PRESENTATION = 'phone-frame' | 'responsive-web'. Default for the prototype demo: 'phone-frame' on desktop (centered 420px device frame), and full-screen on real mobile browsers. 'responsive-web' removes the frame and lets the layout adapt (bottom nav on mobile, top nav or sidebar on wide screens).
The phone frame is a thin wrapper component (PhoneFrame) that can be deleted without touching any screen.

Keep the consumer and admin codebases decoupled so that the next developer can (a) ship only the consumer side as the React Native app, (b) ship only the admin panel as the website, or (c) keep consumer on the web too. Do not let either side depend on the other's UI code.
Everything that is NOT UI (types, validation, calculations, API client, constants) lives in a shared 'src/core' folder with zero React or DOM imports so it can be reused as-is in React Native.
delivery_surfaces.note_on_scope_pdf: The Scope of Work lists 'customer-facing website' as an exclusion (can be added on request). Serving the consumer UI in the browser here is purely for prototype demonstration and must be documented as such in the README.

feature_completeness_standard.goal: This is a prototype to SHOW the customer, but it must also be a WORKING reference implementation. Every feature in the Scope of Work must function end-to-end with real business logic, validation and state changes, so the next developer only replaces the mocked infrastructure (API, auth provider, payment gateway, push) and never has to re-design or re-build features.
rules: No dead buttons, no 'coming soon', no hardcoded screens. Every screen renders from data and every action changes data.
No lorem ipsum or static fake numbers in components. All numbers come from the data layer (outstanding, EMI, breakdown, history, dashboard totals).

Business rules are implemented once in src/core/domain and unit tested, per DuesPlan: plan outstanding = principal + interest + processing fee (breakdowns always add up); consumer total outstanding = sum of active plans; paying an EMI on a plan reduces that plan's outstanding and decrements its remaining EMIs; that plan's next EMI date advances by one month; custom payment cannot exceed that plan's outstanding; 'Pay All' allocates earliest due date first and creates one Payment per plan with a shared transactionRef; a plan reaching zero is closed; due-soon = any plan's next EMI within 7 days; overdue = a plan's next EMI date in the past with outstanding > 0; failed or pending payments never change balances.
Forms: full validation with clear messages (email OR 10-digit Indian mobile, password strength, duplicate mobile/email/account number, amount ranges, CSV row validation).
Every list supports search, filter, sorting and pagination where relevant, plus loading, empty and error states.

Edge cases handled: zero outstanding ('All dues cleared'), inactive consumer cannot log in, disabled card hidden from the app, expired session, double-tap on Pay Now (idempotent), failed payment retry.
Exports really work: CSV/Excel/PDF downloads for dues, collections and EMI schedules, and receipt download.

mock_api_layer.approach: Do not call the Zustand store directly from services. Instead build a typed API client (src/core/api) that makes real fetch() calls to REST endpoints under /api/consumer/* and /api/admin/*, and intercept those calls in the browser with Mock Service Worker (MSW) handlers backed by the persisted store.
mock_api_layer.why: The next developer deletes the MSW handlers, sets VITE_API_BASE_URL to the real server, and the entire UI keeps working because the request and response shapes are already the final contract.
requirements: Every endpoint documented in docs/API_CONTRACT.md has a matching MSW handler with realistic status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422) and error bodies.
Auth uses mock JWT-style tokens sent in an Authorization header; consumer tokens are rejected on /api/admin/* and admin tokens on /api/consumer/* (403).
Add artificial latency (300-600ms) and a dev switch to simulate network errors for testing error states.
MSW is enabled only when VITE_ENABLE_MOCKS=true.

testing.unit: Vitest for src/core/domain (payment rules, EMI calculation, CSV validation, formatters, due status).
testing.component: React Testing Library for login, pay dues, bulk upload and consumer form.
testing.e2e: Playwright smoke tests: consumer login, pay EMI (mock success), see it in admin payments; admin updates EMI date, consumer app reflects it; route separation tests from access_control_and_route_separation; bulk CSV upload; card disable/enable.; admin adds a Card EMI plan to a consumer and it appears in the consumer's Your Dues; consumer pays one plan and only that plan changes; Pay All allocation; disabled plan type cannot be assigned.
testing.ci: npm scripts: dev, build, lint, typecheck, test, test:e2e. All must pass before the work is considered done.

definition_of_done: Every item in Scope of Work sections 4 and 5 is implemented and ticked in docs/FEATURE_CHECKLIST.md with the screen/route that delivers it.
All acceptance tests (route separation, payment flow, admin-to-consumer sync) pass.
Only these things are mocked and listed in docs/MOCKED_SERVICES.md: REST backend (MSW), Google sign-in, Razorpay payments, push notifications, SMS/email OTP, file storage for card images.
Each mocked item has a one-paragraph 'how to replace' note.
README explains how to run the prototype in both consumer presentation modes.

multiple_dues_plans.problem_solved: A consumer can have several different EMIs or dues at the same time (for example a loan EMI, a card EMI, a credit card bill, or any other type). The ADMIN decides which types exist, which ones each consumer has, and the amounts. The consumer app must show and let them pay exactly those, with every payment updating the correct plan.

concepts.PlanType: Admin-managed master list (e.g. Loan EMI, Card EMI, Credit Card Bill, Other Dues). Each has name, category (LOAN_EMI | CARD_EMI | CARD_BILL | OTHER), icon and an enabled flag. Admin can add, edit, disable types without code changes. Seed: Loan EMI, Card EMI, Credit Card Bill, Other Dues.
concepts.DuesPlan: One dues item belonging to one consumer and one PlanType. A consumer can have zero, one or many active plans. Each plan has its own outstanding amount, breakdown (principal, interest, processing fee), EMI amount, next EMI date, total/remaining EMIs, tenure, optional linked card, reference number and status (active | closed).

rules: Consumer totals are always derived: total outstanding = sum of active plans' outstanding; Home 'Next EMI' = the plan(s) with the earliest next EMI date (show the combined EMI amount due on that date and the number of plans).
Paying is always against a specific plan, or 'Pay All' which allocates across plans (earliest due date first) and creates one Payment record per plan sharing one transaction reference.
A plan with outstanding 0 is automatically marked closed and disappears from Pay Dues (shown as 'Cleared' in history/EMI schedule).
Admin-created, edited, closed or reassigned plans appear in the consumer app immediately and generate a balance-update notification and an Activity Log entry.
A disabled PlanType hides nothing already assigned but cannot be assigned to new plans.

consumer_app_changes.home: Outstanding card shows the TOTAL across plans. Below Quick Actions add a 'Your Dues' horizontal list of plan cards (type icon, plan title, outstanding, next EMI amount and date, Due Soon pill). Tapping a plan opens Pay Dues preselected on that plan.
consumer_app_changes.pay_dues: Top: a plan selector (chips or list) with each plan's type and outstanding, plus a 'Pay All Dues' option. Breakdown, amount options (Pay Next EMI, Pay Full Outstanding for that plan, Custom Amount) and payment method all apply to the selected plan(s). Show an allocation summary when Pay All is chosen.
consumer_app_changes.payment_history: Each row titled with the plan (e.g. 'Loan EMI Payment', 'Card EMI Payment') and plan reference. Add a filter by plan type next to the existing filters.
consumer_app_changes.consumer_details: EMI Schedule section has a plan selector; schedule, remaining EMIs, tenure and dues summary are shown per selected plan, with a combined summary above it.
consumer_app_changes.receipt: Shows plan type, plan title and reference.

admin_changes.new_module: EMI & Dues Types: manage the PlanType master list (add, edit, enable/disable, icon, category).
admin_changes.dues_updates: Per-consumer page lists all that consumer's plans. Admin can add a plan (choose PlanType, title, reference, amounts, EMI amount, next EMI date, tenure, optional linked card), edit it, close it, or delete it (super_admin only). Every change is logged.
admin_changes.bulk_upload: CSV/Excel template gains columns: account_number, plan_type, plan_reference, outstanding, principal, interest, processing_fee, emi_amount, next_emi_date, total_emis, remaining_emis, tenure_months. Rows upsert by (account_number + plan_reference); unknown plan_type is a row-level error.
admin_changes.payments: Payments list, offline payment form and reports gain a Plan Type / Plan column and filter. Recording an offline payment requires choosing the plan.
admin_changes.dashboard: Outstanding and collections can be broken down by plan type (chart + export).
